messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the video's camera setup to an upper-body shot from a front three-quarter angle. Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Retain the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, and action in the same environment. Only change how the camera captures the scene. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Retain the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, and action in the same environment. Only change how the camera captures the scene. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The character stands on a street, then lifts his blue hair into a topknot, adjusts his vest, and settles back into a standing pose.","camera":"Static medium shot at eye level, framing the character from the thighs up.","clothing":"A white long-sleeved collared shirt under a black sleeveless vest, with a red plaid kilt and a black belt.","hair_color":"Bright blue.","hairstyle":"Short hair that is repeatedly lifted and repositioned into a tall, rounded blue topknot.","identity":"A 3D-rendered Black male character with a slim build and a slight smile.","scene":"A cobblestone street in front of old stone and brick buildings with posters, lampposts, and bollards."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The output begins with a static medium upper-body shot from a front three-quarter angle, closely matching the reference framing and subject placement. The character remains the same 3D-rendered Black male with bright blue hair, white shirt, black vest, and plaid kilt, and performs the same hair-lifting/topknot and vest-adjusting action in the same street environment.
arguments.requested_change: Change the camera to an upper-body shot from a front three-quarter angle, using the reference image for initial viewing direction, subject placement, and framing, while preserving the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, action, environment, and timing.
uncertain: Exact preservation of the action timing and progression cannot be verified precisely from the provided frames.
unexpected_changes: The background storefront signage visible in the source, including the prominent SOAP and COCOA POWDER windows, is not visible in the output framing; the visible street background is shifted to show different buildings and posters.
